summary:
Smart Aero Field is a bilingual (Bengali & English) mobile-first agricultural decision platform for smallholder farmers across all 64 districts of Bangladesh.

Static sowing calendars fail under shifting monsoons and rising heat stress. Smart Aero Field combines NASA Earth observation data to deliver climate-aware crop guidance: an ML risk and best-crop model trained on NASA POWER agroclimatology, live 250 m NDVI and 1 km Land Surface Temperature from NASA MODIS Terra (ORNL DAAC), and live 7-day rainfall from NASA GPM IMERG V07. Planting-window advisories and crop-specific fertilizer doses (kg/bigha) are adapted from BRRI and BARC guidelines across 15 Agro-Ecological Zones covering all 64 districts, with AWD irrigation protocols for rice. A Gemini-powered leaf disease scanner and a 24/7 Bangla AI agronomist complete the toolkit.

By turning complex satellite data into clear Bangla advice and actionable field recommendations, Smart Aero Field helps farmers protect harvests, reduce wasted water and fertilizer, and build climate resilience.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Smart Aero Field is a bilingual (Bengali & English), mobile-first agricultural intelligence platform built for smallholder farmers across all 64 districts of Bangladesh. It bridges live NASA Earth observation telemetry, national agronomic standards, and multimodal AI into actionable field decisions:

• Live NASA Earth Observation Telemetry:

- NASA POWER Climatology (MERRA-2 / GEOS-FP): Queried via our custom ML inference API (/api/predict) with Day-of-Year (DOY) baseline alignment to estimate district crop suitability, climate risk confidence, and 7-day temperature/rainfall anomalies.

- NASA MODIS Terra (ORNL DAAC REST API): Retrieves live 250m 16-day NDVI (MOD13Q1) vegetation health and 1km 8-day Day Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2) per district with pixel quality filtering and tile tracking.

- NASA GPM IMERG V07 (NASA-USAID SERVIR ClimateSERV): Runs live polygon queries (datatype=227) to compute 7-day accumulated satellite rainfall (mm) and daily precipitation trends.

• Climate-Adaptive Planting Window Advisory (2001–2026): Compares historical (2001–2005) vs. recent (2021–2025) usable-rainfall onset distributions (50mm soil recharge threshold) and Growing Degree Days (GDD Base 10°C) for Aman, Boro, and Aus rice, replacing outdated static sowing calendars with a clear Bangla farmer verdict.

• BARC & BRRI Precision Agronomy: Maps all 64 districts across 15 BARC Agro-Ecological Zones (AEZs) to compute exact crop-specific Urea, TSP, MoP, Gypsum, Zinc, and Boron doses (kg/bigha & kg/ha) for 6 crops, paired with BRRI zone-specific rice varieties (drought, coastal salinity, haor flash-flood, and cold-tolerant) and Alternate Wetting & Drying (AWD) irrigation guidance.

• AI Leaf Disease Scanner & 24/7 Agronomist: Farmers capture leaf or fruit photos on their phone camera for instant multimodal diagnosis via Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (with optional Hugging Face vision cross-validation), receiving bilingual chemical dosages, organic remedies, and preventive guidance, plus a 24/7 AI chat advisor and a Firebase-synced Farm Supplies & Profit/Loss ledger.

Benefits

• Replaces guesswork and outdated sowing calendars with satellite-backed transplanting windows.

• Converts abstract satellite metrics into practical local units (kg/bigha fertilizer doses and BDT market rates).

• Cuts fertilizer waste and saves 25–30% irrigation water through BARC AEZ dosing and BRRI AWD water scheduling.

• Enables rapid, on-field crop disease detection without needing to travel miles to an extension office.

Intended Impact

Bangladesh has over 16.5 million smallholder farming households highly exposed to shifting monsoons, salinity intrusion, flash floods, and heat stress. By making NASA Earth science accessible in native Bengali on everyday smartphones, Smart Aero Field aims to protect seasonal harvests, lower input costs, prevent overuse of nitrogen fertilizers, and strengthen climate resilience at the grassroots level.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

• Languages & Frontend: TypeScript 5.8, React 19, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons, Motion.

• Backend & Serverless Infrastructure: Node.js, Express (tsx), Vercel Serverless Functions (/api/*), Render-hosted ML inference microservice.

• Earth Observation & AI SDKs: NASA ORNL DAAC MODIS REST API, NASA SERVIR ClimateSERV REST API, NASA POWER climatology, @google/genai (Gemini 2.5 / 2.0 / 1.5 Flash), Hugging Face Inference API (dima806/crop_leaf_diseases_detection).

• Database & Auth: Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore.

• Hardware: Developed on standard workstations and engineered for budget Android smartphones with a mobile camera and browser.

How Our Project Is Creative

Instead of building another raw satellite dashboard meant only for researchers, we created a farmer-first translation layer: pairing live NASA MODIS/IMERG/POWER data directly with Bangladesh's 15 BARC AEZs, BRRI stress-tolerant rice protocols, local "bigha" measurements, and instant bilingual AI pathology so any farmer can act on space data within seconds.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

• Rural Connectivity & Cold-Start Resilience: To prevent failures on slow rural networks or serverless timeouts, we built self-contained API handlers, a browser-direct CORS fallback to NASA ORNL DAAC and ClimateSERV, multi-model Gemini failover, and regional BARC baseline fallbacks.

• Ecological Diversity Across 64 Districts: Farming conditions in drought-prone Barind (Rajshahi), coastal saline belts (Satkhira/Barishal), and flash-flood Haor basins (Sylhet/Sunamganj) differ drastically—so every district uses localized AEZ soil factors and stress-adapted BRRI recommendations.

• Language & Usability: Full বাংলা (Bengali) and English toggle, high-contrast mobile cards, camera-first workflow, and plain-language final verdicts ensure accessibility for farmers with varying technical literacy.
